speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please sit down; I understand your wife is concerned about your recent behavior. Can you tell me exactly what strange or agitated actions you have been doing lately, and when did they start?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia.

Thank you for that detailed history; your description of paranoia regarding the NSA, auditory hallucinations of mind control, and the withdrawal of social functioning aligns with a psychotic disorder. Given the 6-week duration of active symptoms and the presence of functional decline, I need to confirm if you have experienced any mood episodes like mania or severe depression to rule out schizoaffective disorder. Are there any family members who have had a similar psychiatric history?
